journal: Finished my presentation!
Mom saved me dinner.
Missed them again today.
Trying again tomorrow.
That was completely unfair.
How did that happen?
I can't decide anything.
Quiet tea before bed.
Got the internship offer.
She checked in on me.
The room feels emptier.
One small step forward.
They ignored my message again.
I saw Saturn's rings.
Everything feels a little off.
I woke before everyone else and made coffee while the apartment was still quiet. Nothing special happened, but I liked having a slow start. I watched the light move across the kitchen floor.
The interview was harder than I expected, and I stumbled on one answer. Then the recruiter told me my portfolio stood out and invited me to the next round. I keep replaying both parts in my head.
My roommate noticed I had skipped lunch and left a bowl of soup by my door. We have both been busy and barely talked this week. That little gesture stayed with me all afternoon.
I packed the last box from my old room today. I know moving is the right choice, but closing the door felt heavier than I expected. The new place is exciting and unfamiliar at the same time.
I apologized for how I spoke yesterday. The conversation was uncomfortable, but they listened and we agreed to try again. I still feel bad, although the distance between us seems smaller.
The group submitted our work without adding my name. I asked about it twice and nobody answered until the deadline passed. Now they are acting as if it was a harmless mistake.
The museum had a room where every sound changed the lights on the walls. I stayed much longer than I planned because each corner behaved differently. I want to understand how they built it.
Three people gave me different advice about the same decision. Every option sounds sensible until I imagine choosing it. I made another list, but now I feel less certain than before.
I walked the usual route after dinner and called my sister on the way home. We talked about groceries, work, and a show we both watch. It was an ordinary evening, and that was enough.
We finally launched the project after weeks of late nights. I am proud of the team and relieved that it works, but I will miss our daily calls. Tomorrow I get to sleep in.
I was embarrassed that I forgot her birthday, but she laughed and said my late card was still sweet.
I am happy for my friend, but hearing their news reminded me of what I lost.
The test result was better than last time, although I am scared the progress will not last.
I wanted to celebrate my promotion, then found out my closest teammate was laid off.
The ending surprised me and I loved it, but I still cannot tell what the last scene meant.
Part of me wants to accept the offer, and part of me wants everything to stay the same.
The trip was beautiful, and I am also glad to be back in my own quiet room.
I won the contest, but seeing the runner-up cry made the moment feel strange.
He brought flowers to apologize, and I appreciate the effort even though I am not ready to forgive him.
Looking at old photos made me smile and then suddenly miss everyone.
I cried after therapy, but for once it felt like something had loosened instead of broken.
I am furious they canceled, but honestly I was nervous about going anyway.
I cannot stop thinking about the question, even though not knowing the answer makes me uneasy.
I feel relieved the decision is over and disappointed that it was not mine to make.
The house is finally quiet, but I keep wondering whether I forgot something important.
My friends surprised me with dinner; I laughed all night and felt a little guilty they paid for everything.
I was worried about him, then he called to say he was safe and thanked me for checking.
I expected to feel only sad at graduation, but I am proud too.
Today was exhausting, yet finishing one task made tomorrow feel possible.
Their apology sounded sincere, which somehow made me both calmer and more upset.
I took the bus to campus and arrived at nine.
Washed the sheets and put them back on the bed.
The meeting moved from two o'clock to three.
I bought rice, tomatoes, and soap after work.
The package is scheduled to arrive on Thursday.
I watered the plants and opened the window.
Lunch was noodles and an apple.
I replied to three emails before noon.
The library closed at its usual time.
I charged my phone and set an alarm.
I am not angry; I just need them to stop interrupting me.
It was not surprising, but I still want to know why it happened.
I do not regret saying no, even if I keep thinking about it.
I was not bored; I was enjoying having nothing to do.
I cannot say I hated the party; I actually stayed until the end.
She did not ask for praise; she quietly fixed the problem for everyone.
I am not disappointed in her, only in how the day turned out.
The pain is not gone, but it no longer decides my whole day.
I do not dislike the idea; I dislike being rushed into it.
I was not confused by the answer; it just opened three more questions.

I kept checking the message because the good news did not quite feel real yet.
He remembered the tiny detail I mentioned months ago.
I set two plates before remembering I only needed one.
I noticed I went the whole morning without rehearsing that old conversation.
I smiled through the meeting and wrote down exactly what they said.
The more I read, the larger the question seemed to become.
I opened the application form three times and closed it each time.
For once, the silence did not need to be filled.
Everyone else cheered, and I realized I had been holding my breath.
She moved her umbrella so there was room for me underneath.
I almost sent the photo to them before remembering we do not talk anymore.
I left the unopened letter on the table and went outside instead.
